pages.text: "Time for an errand!" At the last stop, Bami would take a bundle of tickets alone to the stationmaster's hut at the platform's end. They bounced with an empty bundle on their back. "Everything packed?" Dad asked. "Yes!" Bami rushed off.
Dad shook the bundle lightly with his beak. Empty! "Looks rather flat." Bami had forgotten to pack in their excitement. "Can't I just go?" they pouted.
Dad asked, "What if the stationmaster asks for tickets and you have none?" Bami pictured the bull tilting his head, flag in hand, while Bami searched an empty bundle. "That wouldn't be good..."
Dad sat beside Bami at the table. "Pack what you need for the errand, one thing at a time. Shall we count together?" Bami tilted their head. "One at a time?"
Dad lined up a ticket bundle, a hat, and a lunchbox. "These three will get you ready. Tickets, hat, lunchbox—ready!" Bami tapped each with their beak and repeated the names.
"Let's put them in one by one." Bami held the bundle open with a foot. First, they picked up the tickets in their beak.
Tickets in! Hat in! Lunchbox in! Bami counted with Dad. "One, tickets! Two, hat! Three, lunchbox! Ready!" The bundle grew plump.
Bami pulled and tied the cord with their beak, then put the bundle on their back. "Nothing missing now!" Wings wide, they hopped onto the platform. Reeds swayed and the autumn sea sparkled beyond.
The bull stationmaster waited at his hut, waving a flag. Bami took each item out and lined it up. "One, tickets! Two, hat! Three, lunchbox!" "All ready!" He received the tickets and laughed.
Back on the train, Dad cuddled Bami. "You packed and went all by yourself, Conductor Bami!" Counting meant nothing was forgotten. Tickets, hat, lunchbox—ready! Toot! The train left the last stop.
